feedback: If a child doubts the rice will jump from sound alone, have them predict then test, and notice the rice moving without anything touching or blowing on it.
If a child says 'only vibrating things make sound — a sound can't make anything else vibrate', point to the fluttering paper and jumping rice as evidence the link runs both ways.
Connect back: the sound travelling through the air sets the drum skin (and the rice resting on it) or the paper moving — that is sound making matter vibrate.
activities.intendedInsight: Sound carries energy that can shake things, so the link runs both ways: vibration makes sound, and sound makes matter vibrate.
learnerActions: Rest a few grains of rice on a drum skin. Predict what will happen to the rice when you shout right next to the drum (without touching it) — and say why before you try.
Play a loud, low sound from a speaker near the drum, or shout beside it without touching or blowing on it, and watch whether the rice jumps (the sound may need to be loud and close).
Hold a light paper flag or small strip of paper in front of a speaker playing a loud, low sound; watch whether it flutters, and compare with the speaker switched off.
Explain what pushed the rice / fluttered the paper, and what this shows about sound.
activities.title: The reverse direction: sound makes things vibrate
